messages:
nina: quick heads-up — we're seeing reconciliation gaps where billing events don't join to ingest for long-lived chat sessions. suspect tokenizer is mutating attribution keys (appends `#vX`).
sam: any small repro trace you can drop here?
nina: yup, sanitized:
```
ingest: { session: s-901, fingerprint: fp-901, attribution: tenant:acme }
tokenizer: { session: s-901, fingerprint: fp-901, attribution: tenant:acme#v2 }
billing: { session: s-901, fingerprint: fp-901, attribution: tenant:acme }
```
join failed because tokenizer appended `#v2`.
jordan: so non-canonical keys crossing services. is this limited to async tokenization paths?
nina: mostly yes. tokenizer appends heuristic suffix to reduce collision risk when running multiple tokenizer instances in parallel. ingest doesn't strip or normalize.
tara: do we have a stable provenance_id in the ingest envelope we can rely on instead of attribution strings?
evan: provenance_id exists for chunked/streamed requests, but it's optional and older clients don't always include it. can't rely on it universally.
sam: quick brainstorm on fixes: 1) canonicalize at ingest (strip suffixes) — adds CPU to hot path; 2) tokenizer emits canonical_attribution and a mapping sidecar event that audit can consume — keeps ingest light; 3) fallback joins on fingerprint+session combination — brittle for replays.
jordan: (1) increases risk on ingest latency and expands deploy surface. (2) shifts trust to tokenizer but gives explicit mapping events we can persist to audit logs. (3) is unsafe for edge cases.
ops-bot: note: any ingest hot-path change will require a canary plan across ~12 services. :warning:
tara: for compliance/playback we should record an immutable mapping event: `mapping: { original_attribution -> canonical_attribution }` so offline replays can reconcile.
nina: proposal: implement option (2) as follows: tokenizer will compute canonical_attribution (stable form without suffix), include it in the tokenizer output, and also emit a sidecar mapping event to `audit.mappings` topic. ingest will accept canonical_attribution if present and persist it alongside the raw attribution. If missing, ingest will write the event to a postprocess queue and mark it `needs-mapping`.
evan: tradeoffs: extra fanout/storage vs keeping ingest CPU low. we also get better offline auditability. i'm leaning +1 for sidecar mapping.
sam: i can spike a mapping-event schema and a producer harness to measure QPS/fanout and storage cost. will aim for a small perf run.
jordan: i'll prototype the postprocess consumer to reconcile ledger entries when mappings arrive late and add metrics for unmapped count and reconcile latency.
tara: i'll write an audit playbook: how to replay mapping events, how to run a one-off ledger reconcile, and runbook for missing mappings.
nina: can we get a spike + playbook by EOW? sam, you own the spike?
sam: yes. will put up a PR with the schema, perf numbers, and a canary/rollout plan if we touch ingest behavior. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: reminder: include canary steps and rollback criteria in the PR for any change that touches ingest behavior.
